mechanism: Investigational once-weekly subcutaneous triple hormone receptor agonist that activates GIP, GLP-1, and glucagon receptors.
development_status: NCT06383390 is an active-not-recruiting, event-driven Phase 3 cardiovascular and kidney outcomes trial in adults with BMI at least 27 kg/m2 and ASCVD and/or CKD. Retatrutide is not FDA-approved; Lilly states it is legally available only to participants in Lilly clinical trials.
expected_launch_window: ASCVD/CV-kidney outcomes label: 2030+; obesity launch could occur earlier if separate registrational trials support filing and approval
clinical_summary: The assigned TRIUMPH-Outcomes study randomizes about 10,000 adults to escalated retatrutide up to maximum tolerated dose or placebo and measures time to composite serious cardiovascular events and major kidney events over about 248 weeks. Separate retatrutide data support a strong obesity/cardiometabolic profile: Phase 2 showed up to 24.2% mean weight reduction at 48 weeks, and Lilly's TRIUMPH-1 Phase 3 topline release reported 28.3% mean weight reduction at 80 weeks with 12 mg plus significant improvements in waist circumference, non-HDL cholesterol, triglycerides, systolic blood pressure, and hsCRP. Direct ASCVD outcomes efficacy is not yet available.
safety_summary: No NCT06383390 outcomes results are posted. Lilly's TRIUMPH-1 topline safety profile was generally consistent with incretin-based therapies, with nausea, diarrhea, constipation, vomiting, upper respiratory tract infection, dysesthesia, and urinary tract infection reported more often with retatrutide than placebo; adverse-event discontinuations were 4.1%, 6.9%, and 11.3% for 4 mg, 9 mg, and 12 mg versus 4.9% with placebo. Tirzepatide/Zepbound analog labeling supports monitoring for thyroid C-cell tumor risk/contraindications, severe GI reactions, dehydration-related acute kidney injury, gallbladder disease, pancreatitis, hypersensitivity, hypoglycemia with insulin or secretagogues, diabetic retinopathy complications, peri-procedural aspiration risk, and oral-drug absorption issues.
management_tools: Specialty pharmacy or tightly managed pharmacy-benefit distribution
Prior authorization tied to final FDA-labeled population, BMI threshold, established ASCVD/CKD criteria, and background standard-of-care cardiometabolic therapy
Quantity limits aligned to once-weekly dosing and approved titration schedule
Continuation criteria based on tolerability, adherence, and weight/cardiometabolic response until outcomes-specific criteria are available
Avoid concomitant GLP-1, GIP/GLP-1, or other incretin-based obesity therapy unless future labeling supports combination use
Safety documentation for pancreatitis, severe GI disease/gastroparesis, gallbladder events, renal function during dehydration, MTC/MEN2 contraindications, and diabetes-medication hypoglycemia risk
Budget-impact surveillance for broad ASCVD/CKD obesity uptake, employer benefit exclusions, and analog GLP-1 cardiovascular-risk-reduction coverage criteria
evidence_gaps: NCT06383390 has no posted cardiovascular or kidney outcomes results.
Retatrutide has no FDA-approved U.S. label and no direct U.S. price.
Expected ASCVD launch timing is derived from an estimated February 2029 primary completion date plus a typical Phase 3 filing/review lag.
Available efficacy and safety results come from obesity-focused Phase 2 and TRIUMPH-1 studies, not the assigned ASCVD/CKD outcomes trial.
Final labeled indication may be obesity, ASCVD risk reduction, kidney outcomes, or narrower subgroups depending on trial results and regulatory review.
Annual cost uses Zepbound/tirzepatide analog pricing; retatrutide could launch at a premium or with different direct-pay and rebate dynamics.

sources.title: The Effect of Retatrutide Once Weekly on Cardiovascular Outcomes and Kidney Outcomes in Adults Living With Obesity (TRIUMPH-Outcomes)
supports: Sponsor is Eli Lilly and Company.
Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, event-driven trial.
Overall status is active, not recruiting; estimated enrollment is 10,000 participants.
Population includes adults with BMI at least 27 kg/m2 and ASCVD and/or CKD.
Retatrutide arm receives escalated subcutaneous doses up to maximum tolerated dose; comparator is placebo.
Primary outcomes include time to serious cardiovascular composite events and time to major kidney composite events.
Estimated primary completion and study completion are February 2029.

sources.title: A Study of Retatrutide (LY3437943) in Participants Who Have Obesity or Overweight
supports: TRIUMPH-1 is a Phase 3 retatrutide study in obesity or overweight.
Enrollment was about 2,335 participants.
Primary completion was April 6, 2026 and study completion was May 2026.
Primary outcome includes percent change from baseline in body weight.

sources.title: A Study of LY3437943 in Participants Who Have Obesity or Are Overweight
supports: Completed Phase 2 retatrutide/LY3437943 study sponsored by Eli Lilly and Company.
Randomized 338 participants with obesity or overweight.
Primary outcome was mean percent change from baseline in body weight at Week 24.
Studied once-weekly subcutaneous LY3437943 doses up to 12 mg.

sources.title: Lilly's triple agonist, retatrutide, delivered powerful weight loss in pivotal Phase 3 obesity trial
supports: Retatrutide described as investigational, first-in-class GIP, GLP-1, and glucagon triple hormone receptor agonist.
TRIUMPH-1 reported 19.0%, 25.9%, and 28.3% mean weight reduction at 80 weeks for 4 mg, 9 mg, and 12 mg versus 2.2% with placebo.
Lilly reported improvements in waist circumference, non-HDL cholesterol, triglycerides, systolic blood pressure, and hsCRP.
Common adverse events included nausea, diarrhea, constipation, vomiting, and upper respiratory tract infection.
Dysesthesia and urinary tract infections were more frequent with retatrutide than placebo and were generally mild to moderate.
Lilly states retatrutide is legally available only to participants in Lilly clinical trials.

sources.title: Lilly's phase 2 retatrutide results published in The New England Journal of Medicine show the investigational molecule achieved up to 17.5% mean weight reduction at 24 weeks in adults with obesity and overweight
supports: Phase 2 study met the primary endpoint with up to 17.5% mean weight reduction at 24 weeks.
Secondary endpoint showed up to 24.2% mean weight reduction at 48 weeks.
Lilly reported GI side effects were most common, generally mild to moderate, and usually occurred during dose escalation.
Exploratory cardiometabolic improvements included systolic and diastolic blood pressure, triglycerides, LDL cholesterol, total cholesterol, HbA1c, fasting glucose, and insulin.

sources.title: ZEPBOUND (tirzepatide) Prescribing Information
supports: Zepbound is a GIP and GLP-1 receptor agonist administered subcutaneously once weekly.
Maintenance dosing for weight reduction is 5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg once weekly; maximum dosage is 15 mg once weekly.

Label warnings support safety management for thyroid C-cell tumor risk, severe GI reactions, acute kidney injury due to volume depletion, gallbladder disease, pancreatitis, hypersensitivity, hypoglycemia, diabetic retinopathy complications, aspiration risk, and oral-drug interactions.
Common adverse reactions include nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, constipation, abdominal pain, dyspepsia, injection-site reactions, fatigue, hypersensitivity reactions, eructation, hair loss, and GERD.

sources.title: Information for Colorado Prescribers of Prescription Drugs - Zepbound (tirzepatide) injection
supports: Lilly disclosure states WAC is the listed price to the distribution channel before discounts, rebates, or chargebacks.
Zepbound pen WAC is $1,086.37 for a pack of four pens across listed strengths.
The disclosure states there are no generic prescription drugs available from the same therapeutic class.
Direct-to-patient vial prices are listed separately and are not WAC.

sources.title: Zepbound Cost Information | With or Without Insurance
supports: Lilly pricing page states list price is also referred to as WAC.
Patient pharmacy cost may differ based on insurance, pharmacy charges, discounts, and financial assistance.
Lilly direct-to-patient price is not WAC and is available only for cash-paying patients.

sources.title: FDA Approves First Treatment to Reduce Risk of Serious Heart Problems Specifically in Adults with Obesity or Overweight
supports: FDA approved Wegovy to reduce risk of cardiovascular death, heart attack, and stroke in adults with cardiovascular disease and obesity or overweight.
Wegovy provides a regulatory analog for an obesity medicine with cardiovascular risk reduction evidence and labeling.
The approval demonstrates payer-relevant precedent for MACE risk-reduction claims in obesity plus established cardiovascular disease.

sources.title: Weight Loss - Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Agonists Prior Authorization Policy
supports: Cigna policy covers weight-loss GLP-1 agonists including Wegovy and Zepbound with prior authorization.
Adult obesity criteria include BMI at least 30 or BMI at least 27 with weight-related comorbidity and concurrent behavioral modification/reduced-calorie diet.
Continuation criteria for Zepbound include at least 5% baseline weight loss and continued behavioral modification/reduced-calorie diet.
The policy includes a major adverse cardiovascular event risk-reduction pathway for Wegovy in established cardiovascular disease with overweight or obesity.
The policy discourages concomitant use with GLP-1 or GLP-1/GIP agonists.

expected_launch_window.value: ASCVD/CV-kidney outcomes label: 2030+; obesity launch could occur earlier if separate registrational trials support filing and approval
expected_launch_window.method: Used NCT06383390 estimated February 2029 primary completion date and added approximately 12-14 months for outcomes analysis, filing, and FDA review; separately noted that obesity registrational trials are reading out earlier.
expected_launch_window.explanation: The ASCVD/CV-kidney indication depends on the long event-driven outcomes trial, so an outcomes-specific launch before 2030 is unlikely. Earlier obesity approval could precede ASCVD labeling because TRIUMPH-1 has completed and Lilly expects more Phase 3 obesity-program results.

annual_cost_range.method: Used Zepbound/tirzepatide as the closest marketed Lilly incretin analog. Low equals $1,086.37 WAC per four-pen fill times 12 monthly fills. High equals $1,086.37 times 13 28-day fills.
annual_cost_range.explanation: Retatrutide is unpriced. Zepbound is a once-weekly Lilly incretin obesity therapy with public WAC disclosure, making it the most relevant current analog before any retatrutide pricing, rebate, device, or access strategy is known.

clinical_differentiation.method: Weighted first-in-class triple agonist mechanism, Phase 2 and TRIUMPH-1 magnitude of weight loss, cardiometabolic risk-factor improvements, and dedicated 10,000-participant CV/kidney outcomes trial against the lack of direct outcomes data.
clinical_differentiation.explanation: Retatrutide could be highly differentiated if the weight-loss and risk-factor effects translate into ASCVD and kidney event reduction, but the key outcomes evidence is still pending.

budget_impact.method: Combined chronic annual incretin analog WAC around $13K-$14K with a large potential obesity plus established ASCVD/CKD eligible population and likely long duration of therapy.
budget_impact.explanation: Even with PA and benefit-design controls, uptake in ASCVD/CKD patients with BMI at least 27 could create broad recurring spend if outcomes data support labeling and coverage.

disruption_risk.method: Balanced high clinical and budget-impact potential against a February 2029 outcomes completion date, no current approval, no posted outcomes results, and mature GLP-1 management analogs.
disruption_risk.explanation: The asset is not near an ASCVD launch, but a positive outcomes study could shift cardiometabolic pathway management and obesity-drug coverage for high-risk cardiovascular populations.

recommended_action.method: Matched action intensity to non-imminent ASCVD outcomes timing while flagging need to track earlier obesity filings, TRIUMPH-3/other readouts, and analog payer controls.
recommended_action.explanation: Routine monitoring is appropriate now; preparation should escalate when retatrutide files for obesity, when ASCVD/kidney outcomes mature, or when payer-relevant pricing and label details become visible.

quality_flags: No direct retatrutide price found; cost estimate uses Zepbound/tirzepatide analog WAC.
No FDA approval or U.S. label identified for retatrutide as of 2026-05-28.
Assigned ASCVD/CKD outcomes trial has estimated completion in February 2029 and no posted results.
Clinical differentiation relies on obesity-study efficacy and cardiometabolic risk-factor data, not demonstrated ASCVD event reduction.
Potential earlier obesity approval could precede the ASCVD outcomes indication and affect real-world use before outcomes labeling.
